main_issue: Whether and when Agent D can cook strong-smelling devil curry given the smell affecting A's calls, B's room and C's laundry

A-B.evidence: Both complained about the smell (turns 1-2); B later said the smell was fine with door shut (13) and A accepted the Tue/Thu after-7 plan (26), but they never addressed each other.

A-C.evidence: A wanted a ban or weekend-only (1, 5, 10); C proposed cooking on non-laundry days (19) and A added the after-7 condition (22), then accepted the Tue/Thu after-7 plan (26).

A-D.evidence: A first asked for no strong-smelling food, then weekends (5). D proposed a fan, then offered Tue/Thu after 7 (25); A: 'after 7 is fine' (26).

B-C.evidence: C: 'that doesn't help the laundry' (14); B: 'You're right' (15). C's schedule leaves B's concern unaddressed, but B did not object.

B-D.evidence: D asked B whether the weekend would help (6); B said the day makes no difference (8), then said closing the door makes it fine (13). D settled on the Tue/Thu after-7 plan without B objecting.

C-D.evidence: C objected to the smell in the laundry and the fan (3, 16) and asked for non-laundry days (19). D agreed: 'That works for me' (20), and C: 'that works. Thanks' (21).
